Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment findings consistent with DDx:
  - Acute viral upper respiratory infection with possible acute bronchitis (High likelihood)
  - ACE inhibitor–induced cough (Medium likelihood; on lisinopril)
  - Acute sinusitis with postnasal drip contributing to cough (Medium likelihood)
  - Allergic rhinitis with postnasal drip (Low likelihood given green discharge and febrile sensation)
  - Endocrine/metabolic predisposition to infection (diabetes) as a contributing factor (Moderate)
- Plan summary:
  - Educate that most respiratory infections are viral and self-limiting; home monitoring recommended
  - Temperature monitoring: Obtain a thermometer and check temperature; consider red flags
  - If fever persists or worsens (temperature 37.5–38 C or higher) or cough worsens, or if coughing up purulent phlegm, hemoptysis, or new shortness of breath occurs, re-contact
  - Supportive care: Lemon sips 2–3 times daily to soothe throat; maintain fluids; rest
  - Cough management: Cough syrup not advised during the day; if significant nighttime coughing prevents sleep, small amount for sleep may be used
  - Paracetamol-containing products: Do not use additional paracetamol-containing products with lemon sips
  - Diabetes & hypertension: Ensure regular GP-ordered diabetes and blood pressure follow-up; monitor symptoms closely due to increased risk of bacterial superinfection in diabetes
  - Antibiotics: Potentially consider antibiotics if symptoms fail to resolve or worsen or red flags develop
  - Medication review: Consider whether lisinopril could contribute to cough; discuss with prescribing clinician if cough persists
  - No imaging or labs ordered today
